The Prime Minister has instructed his attorneys to file a defamation lawsuit against the left-wing newspaper Haaretz, Shlomi Eldar, and additional parties who fabricated a false allegation against the Prime Minister that never happened.

Contrary to the claim, from the beginning of September until October 7, no conversation took place between the Prime Minister and the President of the United Arab Emirates.

As a rule, diplomatic conversations between the Prime Minister and the UAE President take place exclusively at the Prime Minister’s Office, through a UAE representative who comes to the office with a special encrypted device.

All such conversations are documented.

Eldar himself said yesterday evening in an interview with Channel 12 that the conversation he claims took place—and during which he claims the Prime Minister was given a warning—was conducted in this manner.

However, a thorough review not only of the Prime Minister’s call logs but also of entry records for the Prime Minister’s Office during this period found no record of any UAE representative entering the office.

It is impossible to enter the Prime Minister’s Office without being documented and registered by the security personnel at the facility.

Eldar also lied when he said that Egypt had warned the Prime Minister about a possible attack, a claim that was already refuted at the beginning of the war.

All of this proves that this is a malicious fabrication with clear political timing, as part of the left’s election campaign, and there will be more such false allegations.

This fabrication is intended to distract from what the public already understands:

Ronen Bar and Herzi Halevi saw all the warning signs many hours before the attack began. If, instead of worrying about a miscalculation, they had instructed the IDF, the Shin Bet, and the community security squads to act preemptively, and if they had informed Prime Minister Netanyahu in time, the horrific massacre could have been prevented.

High-profile elimination in western Gaza City

Gazan sources report that earlier today, the IDF eliminated a senior member of Hamas’s military wing—Farah Hamed—in a motorcycle strike on Al-Rashid Street in western Gaza City.
Hamed, 43, was one of the leaders of the Silwad cell (Ramallah district), who was released in the Shalit deal in 2011 and deported to the Strip.

Hamed was arrested in 2004 and sentenced to three life terms for his role in the attack near the village of Ein Yabrud, in which three Duchifat fighters fell:
Staff Sergeant Erez Idan, 20, from Rishon LeZion
Sergeant Elad Polak, 19, from Kiryat Motzkin
Sergeant Roy Yaakov Salomon, 21, from Tel Aviv
A fourth soldier was wounded in the attack.

The Silwad cell was also responsible for the shooting attack in August 2003 that killed Shalom Har-Melech (husband of Knesset member Limor Son Har-Melech). The same cell also murdered Esther Galia in November 2002 and Zvi Goldstein in June 2003.

After his deportation to the Strip in the Shalit deal, Hamed became a leading force in Hamas’s West Bank headquarters—which directed attacks in Judea and Samaria from the Gaza Strip.

An important circle was closed today.

‏גורמים בסביבתו של יו״ר הפרלמנט מוחמד באקר קאליבאף מספרים כי הוא מגדיר את המצב באיראן נואש: המצור האמריקני עובד, המטבע קורס, האינפלציה גבוהה, אין מספיק כסף והמשטר מתקשה לשלוט באוכלוסייה. לדבריו, הנזק מהמלחמה נראה כמעט בלתי ניתן לתיקון.

‏קאליבאף אומר כי הממשלה ומשמרות המהפכה טעו בהערכת טראמפ. הם לא האמינו שיוכל להחזיק את הלחץ לאורך זמן, וכעת מבינים שהוא מצא את נקודת החולשה של איראן. לדבריו, המשטר מתקשה אפילו לקרוא את הצעד הבא שלו.

‏הוא טוען גם כי איראן איבדה למעשה את השליטה במצר הורמוז וכמעט לא נותרו לה קלפי מיקוח.

‏כששואלים אותו מה הפתרון, תשובתו: מלחמה — ועדיף קרוב לבחירות האמצע בארה״ב, בתקווה שטראמפ יאבד את השליטה בשני בתי הקונגרס, ייחלש וייאלץ לחזור למשא ומתן.

‏והביקורת שלו מופנית במיוחד כלפי אחמד וחידי: קאליבאף טוען כי הקו הנוקשה שמוביל מפקד משמרות המהפכה מסכן את איראן, וכי כל עוד הקו הזה לא ישתנה — המדינה תמשיך להידרדר.

‏קאליבאף עצמו אינו סבור שהוא יעד של ישראל או ארה״ב. לדבריו, הוא ואחרים הם מהיחידים שעוד מנסים להכניס היגיון לקו של משמרות המהפכה — והאמריקנים יודעים זאת.

Former Strategic Affairs Minister Ron Dermer, speaking at the MEAD Conference in Washington, addressed a question about the alleged conversation between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the President of the United Arab Emirates before October 7:

“Did such a conversation take place? No.

Had there been a conversation, I would have been part of it, because one of the tasks assigned to me was expanding the Abraham Accords and strengthening the partnership with the United Arab Emirates.

So in all the conversations between the prime minister and Mohammed bin Zayed, the UAE leader, I was either privy to the details or on the line during the conversation itself. This conversation did not take place.

And it’s not even a question of the content of the conversation; I don’t think there was a conversation at all. And that content certainly wasn’t discussed.

So I don’t know where they got this story from. I think the Emiratis have been clear that it didn’t happen. We’ve been clear that it didn’t happen. So it’s essentially a fabrication. Just a made-up story.”
